title: Worker: Vector Embedding Indexer indefinitely loops on oldest single page
sum: _run_embedding_refresh queries FetchedPage without checking for missing ChunkEmbeddings, reprocessing the exact same page on every cycle.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/worker.py`, the `_run_embedding_refresh` method is intended to process unindexed pages. However, the query selects `session.query(FetchedPage).order_by(FetchedPage.fetched_at.asc()).first()` without any filter condition.

## Impact
Every 15 minutes when the background worker runs `embedding_refresh`, it fetches the exact same oldest page in the database, re-embeds it, and exits. Newer pages are never indexed by the worker unless manually triggered via the admin portal.

## Proposed Fix
Add a filter checking for pages lacking chunk embeddings:
```python
subq = select(ChunkEmbedding.source_id).where(ChunkEmbedding.model_name == job.model)
row = session.query(FetchedPage).filter(FetchedPage.url.not_in(subq)).order_by(FetchedPage.fetched_at.asc()).first()
```

title: Security: Unescaped f-string queries in prompt version updates
sum: AgentPrompt version queries concatenate raw prompt_type into SQL statements instead of using parameterized bindings.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/config.py:719` and `726`, raw f-strings are used to construct SQL queries:
```python
db.execute_returning_dicts(f"SELECT MAX(version) as mv FROM agent_prompts WHERE prompt_type = '{prompt_type}'")
db.execute(f"UPDATE agent_prompts SET is_head = 0 WHERE prompt_type = '{prompt_type}'")
```

## Impact
If a dynamic or user-supplied prompt type contains quotes or SQL control characters, it causes SQL syntax errors or potential SQL injection.

## Proposed Fix
Use parameterized queries:
```python
db.execute("UPDATE agent_prompts SET is_head = 0 WHERE prompt_type = ?", [prompt_type])
```

title: Security: Stored XSS in Autonomous Agent Wikis & Themed Canvas Pages
sum: Agent wiki markdown and themed canvas pages render raw markdown without HTML sanitization (nh3/bleach) into {{ rendered_body | safe }}.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/routers/agent_pages.py`, agent wiki articles and themed canvas pages render markdown via:
```python
rendered_body = markdown.markdown(
    page.body_markdown or "",
    extensions=["fenced_code", "tables", "nl2br", "toc"],
)
```
and pass it directly to `topic_wiki_page.j2.html` and `agent_page_themed.j2.html` where it is rendered with `{{ rendered_body | safe }}`. Unlike `src/kb_web/routers/pages.py`, no call to `sanitize_html()` or `nh3.clean()` is made.

## Impact
An autonomous topic agent or user-submitted article note containing `<script>`, malicious `<iframe src=...>`, or event handlers (`onload=...`) executes arbitrary scripts whenever a visitor or administrator inspects the living wiki or themed page.

## Proposed Fix
Sanitize `rendered_body` using `sanitize_html(rendered_body)` before passing it to the Jinja template.

title: Security: DOM XSS & Attribute Breakout via Unescaped URLs in Event Handlers
sum: Item URLs containing quotes or control characters break JavaScript string literals in onclick handlers and data attributes.
body:
## Summary In `src/kb_web/templates/view_collection.j2.html:366`: ```javascript card.innerHTML = `... ...`; ``` and in `collection_editor.j2.html:422`: ```javascript

Original Link: ${orig.url}

``` ## Impact If an ingested URL contains single quotes, double quotes, or JavaScript control sequences (e.g. `https://example.com/item');alert(1);//`), interpolating into `removeSingleItem('${item.url}')` causes JavaScript execution or syntax errors when rendering items. ## Proposed Fix Escape URLs using `escapeHtml(item.url)` for attribute values and use `encodeURIComponent()` or `dataset` attributes rather than inline JavaScript string concatenation.

title: Workspace: Folder deletion loop sends N individual requests instead of atomic prefix deletion
sum: Deleting a folder in Workspace IDE executes a client-side loop sending sequential DELETE requests per file instead of using server prefix deletion.

title: Frontend: Jinja Highlighter event listener leak and Jinja filter regex breakage
sum: JinjaHighlighter lacks destroy/cleanup methods for window resize listeners, and regex fails to match Jinja expressions using pipe filters.
body:
## Summary
1. In `src/kb_web/static/js/jinja_highlighter.js`, every instance binds `window.addEventListener('resize', ...)` and `ResizeObserver` without providing a `destroy()` or `disconnect()` method. When editor dialogs or tab views re-render, listeners accumulate, leaking memory.
2. The parameter detection regex `const regex = /\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+)\s*\}\}/g;` only allows alphanumeric characters and dots. If a prompt uses standard Jinja filter expressions like `{{ data.title | default('None') }}` or `{{ data.tags | join(', ') }}`, the regex fails to match or misidentifies the field as invalid.

## Proposed Fix
1. Add a `destroy()` method that removes the window resize listener and disconnects `this.resizeObserver`.
2. Update regex to accommodate Jinja filters: `/\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+)(?:\s*\|[^}]+)?\s*\}\}/g`.

title: Admin: Jinja Highlighter script tag placed after DOMContentLoaded initialization block
sum: admin.j2.html calls initJinjaHighlighter inside DOMContentLoaded at line 1660, but loads jinja_highlighter.js at line 2647.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/templates/admin.j2.html`, the script at line 1660 attempts to initialize all `.agent-jinja-template` textareas:
```javascript
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
    if (typeof window.initJinjaHighlighter === 'function') {
        ...
```
However, `<script src="/static/js/jinja_highlighter.js"></script>` is placed at line 2647, at the very bottom of the template block. In certain browsers or cached states, `DOMContentLoaded` fires before the script has finished executing, leaving `window.initJinjaHighlighter` undefined.

## Proposed Fix
Move `<script src="/static/js/jinja_highlighter.js"></script>` to the `extra_head` block or before the main inline script block, consistent with `evals.j2.html`.

title: Performance: Unindexed per-row ghost stub deletion loop runs on every server startup
sum: ensure_views_and_indexes executes 10 separate DELETE statements per ghost URL in a Python loop every time the server boots.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/models_orm.py:867-884`, `ensure_views_and_indexes(engine)` queries for ghost URLs matching `Archived Item (%` and executes 10 separate `DELETE FROM ... WHERE url = :u` statements sequentially for every ghost URL found on every server boot.

## Impact
Increases server startup latency, especially on larger databases or remote PostgreSQL instances over higher-latency connections.

## Recommendation
Wrap the cleanup into a single batch CTE or set-based DELETE statement, or move it to a one-time Alembic migration script.

title: Performance: Vault Zip unpacker opens individual DB session per note and overwhelms Ollama queue
sum: Unpacking a note vault zip executes a per-file database commit and spawns unbounded concurrent background Ollama tasks.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/routers/notes.py:385-411`, during zip extraction, every single `.md` file opens a new `with db_session() as session:`, executes a `commit()`, and immediately adds `_process_note_in_background` to FastAPI `background_tasks`.

## Impact
Importing a 2,000-note vault causes 2,000 individual database transactions, followed by 2,000 concurrent background workers attempting to hit Ollama simultaneously for tags, titles, and embeddings, resulting in CPU starvation and Ollama timeouts.

## Recommendation
Batch all database insertions in a single transaction, and delegate the post-processing to the asynchronous `autonomous_worker` job queue or a throttled task pool.

title: Performance: Unbounded in-memory scan of all Note records during taxonomy classification
sum: trigger_classify_notes loads every Note record into memory via query.all() before filtering in Python.
body:
## Summary
In `src/kb_web/routers/taxonomy.py:175-180`, the endpoint executes:
```python
all_matching = query.all()
target_notes = [
    n for n in all_matching
    if f"note_{n.id}" not in classified_item_ids and str(n.id) not in classified_item_ids
]
```

## Impact
On vaults with 20,000+ notes, `query.all()` allocates all ORM note instances into Python memory at once, spiking RAM usage and causing garbage collection thrashing.

## Recommendation
Perform the exclusion at the database query level using SQL `NOT IN` or a `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE TaxonomyItem.id IS NULL`.

title: Deprecation: Phase out legacy 10-item partitioning Category Taxonomy State Machine
sum: 1,289 lines of flat category ontology logic locks global additions during partitioning and should be deprecated in favor of 7-tier biological taxonomy.
body:
## Summary
`src/kb_web/taxonomy_state_machine.py` contains 1,289 lines of complex dynamic folder restructuring code. When any category reaches 10 items, it triggers a global lock (`_taxonomy_lock`) and sets `_partitioning_paused = True`, halting additions across the entire application while partitioning items.

## Impact
- Causes intermittent thread contention and delayed web page imports.
- Re-partitions and merges categories ad-hoc, destabilizing category URLs and bookmarks.
- Duplicates and conflicts with the new, structured 7-tier biological taxonomy (`src/kb_web/taxonomy/` and `src/kb_web/context_mesh/`).

## Recommendation
Mark `taxonomy_state_machine.py`, `TaxonomyCategory`, and `TaxonomyItem` as deprecated. Transition `/taxonomy` and `/api/taxonomy/*` to query `TaxonomyEngine` and `taxonomy_entities` coordinates.

title: Deprecation: Fragmented article_embeddings, title_embeddings, and video_embeddings tables
sum: Redundant single-vector tables should be phased out in favor of ChunkEmbedding and context_statements.statement_vector.
body:
## Summary
`models_orm.py` maintains three separate single-vector tables:
- `article_embeddings`
- `title_embeddings`
- `video_embeddings`

Meanwhile, `chunk_embeddings` already stores multi-chunk vectors with document chunk offsets, metadata, and model names for semantic search in PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Qdrant. Furthermore, `context_statements` now provides atomic intent and fact vector search.

## Recommendation
Consolidate document-level search onto `chunk_embeddings` and deprecate the three legacy single-vector tables to reduce write amplification and index overhead during ingestion.

title: Deprecation: Direct sqlite_utils dependency in PostgreSQL-first architecture
sum: sqlite-utils is imported directly in db.py despite PostgreSQL being the primary database and SQLAlchemy managing sessions.
body:
## Summary
`src/kb_web/db.py:18` imports `sqlite_utils.Database` directly in `get_db()`. In the current architecture, all queries, models, and migrations are managed through SQLAlchemy `db_session()` and PostgreSQL `SafeVector`.

## Recommendation
Deprecate `get_db()` and remove `sqlite-utils` from `pyproject.toml` dependencies once remaining CLI commands are migrated to standard SQLAlchemy sessions.

title: Deprecation: SQLAlchemy 2.0 MovedIn20Warning for declarative_base()
sum: Use sqlalchemy.orm.declarative_base() instead of sqlalchemy.ext.declarative.declarative_base() to avoid deprecation warnings.
body:
## Summary
`src/kb_web/models_orm.py:7` imports `declarative_base` from `sqlalchemy.ext.declarative`, triggering `MovedIn20Warning: The declarative_base() function is now available as sqlalchemy.orm.declarative_base()` on every test and server startup.

## Proposed Fix
Change line 4 in `models_orm.py`:
```python
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, declarative_base
```

title: Architecture: Hardcoded magic id=1 assumptions for General Collection
sum: General Collection assumption hardcodes collection_id=1 across database views and queries, creating migration and domain grouping fragility.
body:
## Summary
Throughout `src/kb_web/db.py` and the `vw_page_cards` view definition (`models_orm.py:903`), collection ID 1 is hardcoded as `General Collection` (`ci.collection_id != 1`).

## Impact
If database IDs are re-sequenced or restored from external dumps where collections start at a different sequence, items in the primary collection are miscategorized or hidden from general views.

## Recommendation
Replace hardcoded `id=1` with an explicit boolean flag on the Collection model (e.g. `is_default: bool = False`) or lookup by slug.

title: Code Quality: Naive local datetime instead of timezone-aware UTC
sum: Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) to prevent timezone drift across client and server environments.
body:
## Summary
Across 95 occurrences in the repository, timestamps are generated using `datetime.now().isoformat()` without timezone awareness instead of `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`.

## Impact
Can lead to subtle ordering issues or mismatched timestamps when client and server operate across differing UTC offsets.

title: Reliability: Silent exception swallowing without structured logging
sum: Swallowing exceptions with bare except: pass obscures operational failures in background tasks and database transactions.
body:
## Summary
Over 90 code blocks catch broad `Exception` and execute `pass` without logging the exception details or traceback.

## Recommendation
Add debug or warning logs (`logger.debug(f"Handled exception: {e}", exc_info=True)`) to preserve observability.
